Geographies Served Programs Research, development, and evaluation District Pune State Maharashtra District Pune States Maharashtra An endeavor to create new literature, develop practical and scalable model based on experiential learning of engaging adolescent boys to be gender equitable. Involved in partnerships to support the development of suitable programs to sensitize the boys. Ensures continuous monitoring to evaluate the impact of this program Action for Equality District Pune State Maharashtra District Pune States Maharashtra A community-led program designed for adolescent boys in the age group of 13 to 17. Boys of this age group are impressionable, but can be trained to understand situations and take responsible decisions. The objective is to systematically change the way communities raise boys through a series of structured interventions and systematic monitoring that continues for up to a year. This program helps to raise gender equitable boys by equipping them with knowledge, peer support, skills and leadership abilities. This program is facilitated by a team of dedicated mentors in 20 communities across Pune, India. Project Raise District Pune State Maharashtra District Pune States Maharashtra A program that partners with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), funding organizations, intermediaries and government institutions who are committed to the social outcome of raising gender equitable boys. Participating agencies are provided knowledge and toolkits to deliver programs, evaluate progress and drive collective action towards the desired outcome of making boys gender equitable. Organizations that are working towards raising gender equitable boys can become members of Project Raise. They will have direct access to online and offline training/research material, and can have meaningful engagement with other member organizations. Members can also use the data from other organizations to influence policies. Project Raise has 290 members and over 35 of these member organizations have adopted the approach to raise gender equitable boys. Over 13022 boys have participated in Project Raise. As a result, about 54% of the participants showed high equitable attitude towards women.
